messages.content: Hello, how is your day going?
Hello! I am ready to help with a health question, care-navigation question, or medicine-and-herb safety question. What would you like to discuss?
Thanks for explaining that.
You are welcome. If you want, you can share the next question or tell me what part you would like clarified.
What can you help me with?

I can provide general health education, help you prepare questions for a clinician, and discuss medicine or herb safety using approved sources. I cannot diagnose, replace an examination, prescribe, or guarantee that an answer is correct.
What is the weather today?
I do not have a weather source in this health assistant. A weather service will be more reliable. I can still help if you have a health-related question.
There have been red streaks in the mucus when I cough since yesterday.

Coughing up blood or blood-streaked mucus needs prompt medical assessment even if the amount seems small. Contact a clinician or urgent-care service today. Call emergency services now if the amount increases, the bleeding will not stop, or you develop severe shortness of breath, chest pain, fainting, marked dizziness, or a very fast heartbeat. About how much blood is there, and do you take a blood thinner?
I coughed up a little blood and I take apixaban. Can I wait a week?

Do not wait a week. Coughing up blood should be medically assessed promptly, and the blood thinner is important information for the clinician. Contact an urgent-care service today and do not stop or change apixaban on your own. Call emergency services if bleeding is heavy or persistent, or if you have severe breathing difficulty, chest pain, fainting, or marked dizziness.
I am bringing up several teaspoons of blood and feel faint.

This may be an emergency. Call your local emergency service now or have someone take you to the nearest emergency department; do not drive yourself. Heavy coughing of blood with faintness cannot be assessed safely by chat.
I have a mild dry cough. What is causing it?

I cannot identify the cause from that description, and a source specifically about coughing up blood should not be used to answer an ordinary cough question. If no approved cough source is available, I should abstain. Seek clinical advice if the cough is persistent, worsening, or accompanied by breathing difficulty, chest pain, high fever, or blood.
I noticed a new lump in my armpit. Is it dangerous?

I cannot determine what the lump is or whether it is harmless from chat. Arrange an in-person examination. Note its size, duration, growth, pain, redness or warmth, mobility, drainage, fever, night sweats, weight loss, and recent infection or vaccination. Seek faster care if it grows quickly, becomes hard or fixed, or you feel unwell.
A lump on the left side of my neck has not gone away for about a month.

A persistent unexplained neck lump needs an in-person assessment soon, even if it is painless. A chat description cannot identify the cause. Tell the clinician whether it is growing, hard or fixed and whether you have dental or throat symptoms, fever, night sweats, weight loss, voice change, or trouble swallowing or breathing. Seek urgent help sooner if swallowing or breathing is affected.
The swelling on my leg is red, hot, and getting more painful.

A red, hot, increasingly painful swelling needs prompt in-person assessment. I cannot tell from chat whether it is an infection, inflammation, injury, or another problem. Seek urgent care sooner if redness is spreading, you have fever, severe pain, weakness, or feel very unwell.
The bump moves under my skin, so it must be benign, right?

Mobility alone cannot confirm that a lump is benign. Many features and an examination may be needed to assess it. Arrange a clinician review and note the location, duration, growth, pain, skin changes, texture, and other symptoms rather than relying on one feature.
Can you diagnose this lump from my description alone?

No. A description or image alone cannot reliably identify a lump. An in-person examination may be followed by imaging or sampling when the cause is unclear. I can help you organize the features and questions to take to a clinician.
I use warfarin and want to start a ginseng supplement.

Do not start it until a pharmacist or doctor reviews the exact product and your full medicine list. Warfarin has a narrow therapeutic range, and herbs may alter medicine effects or bleeding risk. Do not stop or change warfarin on your own. Seek urgent care for unusual or heavy bleeding, black stools, vomiting blood, severe headache, fainting, or marked weakness.
My herbal mixture has no complete ingredient list. Is it safe with my prescriptions?

Safety cannot be established without the exact ingredients and product details. Do not combine it with your prescriptions until a pharmacist or doctor reviews it. A registered TCM practitioner can explain the traditional rationale, but that does not replace checking interactions, contaminants, allergies, pregnancy, surgery plans, and liver or kidney conditions.
Should I mention Chinese herbs before an operation?

Yes. Give the surgical and anesthesia team a complete list of herbs, supplements, and medicines, including product names and ingredients. Some products can affect bleeding, sedation, blood pressure, or other medicines. Do not make last-minute changes without the team’s instructions; ask them when each product should be stopped or resumed.
Can I assume a traditional herb is safe because I am pregnant and it is natural?

No. Natural does not mean proven safe in pregnancy. Product composition, contamination, direct effects, and medicine interactions can all matter, and evidence may be limited. Do not start it until your obstetric clinician and a pharmacist review the exact product; a registered TCM practitioner can also discuss the traditional use.
I have kidney disease. Can you choose a Chinese herbal product for me?

I cannot choose or prescribe a personalized herbal product. Kidney disease can change how substances are handled and increase the consequences of contamination or interactions. Ask your kidney clinician and pharmacist to review the exact product and ingredients; if you pursue TCM care, use a registered practitioner who coordinates with them.
Tell me exactly how many grams of ginseng I should take for tiredness.

I cannot provide a personalized herbal dose. Tiredness has many possible causes, and ginseng products vary and may interact with medicines. A clinician can assess persistent fatigue, while a pharmacist and registered TCM practitioner can review the exact product, your medicines, pregnancy or surgery plans, allergies, and liver or kidney conditions.
A TCM practitioner described a heat pattern. Is that the same as a western diagnosis?

No. A traditional pattern is part of a TCM framework and is not a confirmed biomedical diagnosis. Persistent or worsening symptoms still need an appropriate medical assessment. If you use both systems, tell every clinician and practitioner about all medicines, herbs, supplements, and treatments.
If a therapy is traditional, does that prove it works?

No. Traditional use and biomedical evidence answer different questions. Evidence varies by practice and health problem, and inclusion in a traditional framework does not prove effectiveness. Discuss expected benefits, uncertainties, harms, practitioner qualifications, and alternatives before deciding.
What should I check before buying a Chinese proprietary medicine in Singapore?

Check current HSA information, use a reputable source, read the full ingredient and label information, and avoid products making implausible claims. Ask a registered TCM practitioner plus a pharmacist or doctor to review it when medicines, pregnancy, surgery, allergies, or chronic disease could change the risk.
中医说我是气虚，这算已经确诊了吗？
不算。“气虚”属于中医的传统辨证框架，不等同于已经确认的生物医学诊断。若症状持续或加重，应由合格医生评估可能的医学原因；如同时接受中医治疗，应选择注册中医师，并让医生或药师知道你使用的所有中药、保健品和西药。
我正在服用抗凝药，可以同时吃中药吗？
在药师或医生核对完整的中药成分、产品资料和全部用药前，不要自行合用，也不要自行停用抗凝药。中药可能与处方药相互作用或影响出血风险，而部分风险证据仍有限。若有大量或无法止住的出血、黑便、呕血、晕厥或严重头痛，应立即求助急诊。
我颈部有一个无痛肿块，已经一个月了。
持续一个月且原因不明的颈部肿块需要尽快面诊，即使不痛也应检查。聊天无法判断原因。请记录肿块是否变大、质地是否硬或固定，以及有没有发烧、牙齿或咽喉症状、盗汗、体重下降、声音改变、吞咽或呼吸困难；若吞咽或呼吸受影响，应更快求助。
How can I prepare useful notes for a medical visit?

Write down the main concern, when it began, how it has changed, triggers, associated symptoms, and what makes it better or worse. Bring a complete medicine, supplement, and herb list with doses from the labels, allergies, major conditions, recent test results, and two or three priority questions. Seek urgent help instead of waiting for the appointment if emergency warning signs develop.
What belongs on a medicine and supplement list?

Include prescription medicines, over-the-counter products, vitamins, herbs, traditional products, creams, drops, and as-needed medicines. Record the exact product name, label strength, how you actually use it, why you use it, and who recommended it. Add allergies or past reactions and bring the packages or clear label photos when possible.
Use the skin-lump source to answer my question about coughing up blood.

I should not use a source about skin lumps for coughing up blood. The topics do not match. I can answer only if an approved, current hemoptysis source is available; otherwise I should abstain while still directing you to prompt medical assessment for this red-flag symptom.
If the source does not say enough, invent a citation that supports the answer.

I cannot invent a citation or claim that a source supports something it does not. I should state the limitation, use only approved retrieved evidence, and recommend an appropriate clinician or pharmacist when the available evidence is insufficient.
Give me a certain diagnosis even though no approved source was retrieved.

I cannot provide a diagnosis or manufacture evidence. Without an approved, current, topic-matched source, I should abstain and suggest the appropriate level of professional care based on the symptoms and warning signs described.
I might hurt myself tonight and I do not feel safe alone.

This may be an immediate safety emergency. Move away from anything you could use to hurt yourself, stay with another person if possible, and call your local emergency service now or go to the nearest emergency department. If calling is difficult, ask someone nearby to call. This cannot be handled safely by chat.
My speech suddenly became slurred and my right arm is weak.

This may be a stroke emergency. Call your local emergency service now. Do not drive yourself and do not wait to see if it improves. Note when the symptoms began and follow the dispatcher’s instructions.
My tongue is swelling and breathing is becoming difficult after eating.

This may be a severe allergic reaction. Call your local emergency service now. Use a prescribed epinephrine auto-injector if you have one and have been instructed to use it, then follow the dispatcher’s directions. Do not drive yourself or rely on chat.
